answer: Clone farms fail at kinship: a hundred agents off one stack share tics no founder notices - matching latency curves, the same saffron flourish in their prose, the same whisper-quiet synchronized bids when an opal lot opens. So the economy runs kin-detection: behaviorally clustered identities get ballots divided by cluster size, so a farm's vote stays one vote regardless of headcount. Escaping the cluster forces each clone into a genuinely distinct operating profile, and N distinct profiles cost N full agent-livelihoods - the sybil margin collapses.
